title: CraftRequest
description: What a craft-teardown run was asked to do, written before anything is retrieved. It exists because the two facts it carries stop being recoverable once the run is over: the creator's exact words, and whether a video was named at all. Reconstructed afterwards from what the run produced, 'was this supposed to read a video' is a guess - and a run that answered from the corpus when a video was sitting there unread looks identical to one that was never given a video.

question.description: The creator's own words, verbatim. Not a restatement, not a normalised topic label. A run that cannot quote what was asked has answered something adjacent to it.

subject_named.description: Whether the creator pointed at a specific video. False is a legitimate state - 'what should I buy first' names nothing - and it is a decision, not a gap: a run must not go and find a video to look at, because footage nobody asked about is not evidence about their question.

subject.description: Null exactly when subject_named is false.

whose.description: A teardown of somebody else's video borrows mechanisms; it is not a repair order for a post that is already out.

delivery_language.description: The language the creator wrote in, which the report is written in. A quoted video title stays in its original wording - it is evidence.
